question: During the European Council of 21 to 22 March 2024, the decision was taken to open accession negotiations with Bosnia and Herzegovina, following the recommendation by the Commission. The Commission has been invited to prepare the negotiating framework, after which the Council will decide whether to adopt this framework once all relevant steps set out in the Commission’s report of 12 October 2022 have been taken. 1.

Could the Commission confirm that the next formal step in the accession process of Bosnia and Herzegovina – before the adoption of the negotiation framework – is the so-called screening process, during which the negotiating position of Bosnia and Herzegovina will be determined?

Can the Commission confirm that the adoption of a negotiation framework is dependent on the successful completion of the screening phase, and that the latter can therefore not start before this process has been completed?
When will the screening process start and could the Commission provide a timeline for it?
answer: Following the European Council decision of March 2024 to open EU accession negotiations with Bosnia and Herzegovina (1), the Commission is preparing for the next steps, in line with the enlargement methodology. The Commission held a first introductory meeting on 24 April 2024 in Brussels to explain the process ahead, in particular the screening, which is the first stage of accession negotiations.

The Commission provided Bosnia and Herzegovina with explanatory materials and is scheduling questions and answers sessions on the EU acquis, starting with rule of law Chapter 23, in the upcoming period. This will be followed by explanatory meetings on the EU acquis. As per the European Council’s invitation, the Commission is also preparing the negotiating framework for Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The Commission will present it to the Council in due time with a view to its adoption by the Council the moment all relevant steps set out in the Commission’s recommendation of 12 October 2022 are taken.

The Commission continues to encourage Bosnia and Herzegovina to address all relevant steps from its 2022 recommendation (2), so that the Council may be in a position to adopt the negotiating framework and hold the first intergovernmental conference, in line with the European Council decision of March 2024. The Commission continues political contacts at all levels to pass this message.

On 21 March 2024, the European Council decided to open accession negotiations with Bosnia and Herzegovina and invited the Commission to ‘prepare the negotiating framework with a view to its adoption by the Council the moment all relevant steps set out in the Commission’s recommendation of 12 October 2022 are taken’, https://www.consilium.europa.eu/media/70880/euco-conclusions-2122032024.
